PyTorch GRU computes r=σ(Wir x+bir+Whr h+bhr), z=σ(Wiz x+biz+Whz h+bhz), n=tanh(Win x+bin+r⊙(Whn h+bhn)), and h′=(1−z)⊙n+z⊙h. Reset multiplies the recurrent candidate projection **including its bias**, rather than the hidden state before projection. A faithful custom cell must preserve these equations and gate ordering. Multilayer dropout applies between recurrent layers, excluding the last layer. For parity testing, disable dropout, copy parameters, and compare outputs, final states, input gradients and parameter gradients within numerical tolerances; neutralize added time-conditioning terms first. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html)

Padding needs explicit handling: zero embeddings alone do not prevent recurrent state updates. For left-padded histories, preserve each layer’s previous state at padding positions, then read the final nonpadding position; count−1 is incorrect. Packing requires moving valid histories to the beginning before calling pack_padded_sequence, with CPU lengths and separate handling of empty histories. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html) Computationally, custom timestep loops can lose fused recurrent-kernel advantages; precomputing input projections and compiling pointwise operations are candidates to benchmark, not guaranteed speedups. PyTorch reports GRU graph breaks in some compiler versions, so verify the installed version. Compare warmed-up forward/backward throughput and include compilation overhead in the fixed search budget. [Custom RNN optimization](https://pytorch.org/blog/optimizing-cuda-rnn-with-torchscript/), [GRU compiler issue](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/167275), [compiler profiling](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/user_guide/torch_compiler/torch.compiler_profiling_torch_compile.html)
